issues: No integrity problems: no file or network access, no pasted answers. The out-of-fold pass uses only train_smiles/train_y; test labels are never used. The inner GroupKFold shuffle is driven by the seed argument, so it is reproducible.
No invalidating bug. The logic is sound as written.

Cost concern: fit_predict_pair is now called 6 times per fold (5 inner folds + 1 final refit) instead of once, roughly 6x the compute per fold. No job runtime was reported, so I cannot verify it against the 10-minute cap; the job did complete and return a score.

Design weakness (not a bug): the 'hard example' rule thresholds the scaled out-of-fold rank at 0.5, which ignores class balance. Under class imbalance many correctly ordered majority-class molecules get upweighted, which plausibly explains the regression.
Simplicity: the change adds ~30 lines, a helper, two new imports and ~6x runtime while scoring worse. Not worth keeping on the stated 'simpler is better' criterion.

Numbers are consistent with the diff; no claims in the diff comments overstate the result. Recomputed z matches the reported -1.708 (diff -0.0103 / se 0.0060 = -1.72, small rounding difference). Provisional reject is correct.
